transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. Um, I'm here because... well, I guess I've just been having a really hard time lately. I don't want to overreact or anything, but I just can't shake this feeling that I'm... I don't know, a disappointment? 

I'm a registered nurse, and... well, I had a near-miss at work recently. Nobody got hurt, thank goodness, but... I just keep thinking that it proves I'm not cut out for this. That I'm actually a danger to my patients. It's silly, I know, to let one mistake get to me this much, but sometimes I just feel like everyone would be better off without me getting in the way. Does that make sense? I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't be complaining when nothing actually happened.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with loved ones?

Um... maybe a little? I mean, I don't want to sound lazy or anything. I know working and taking classes is tiring for everyone, so I should be able to handle it. But... I used to always clear my head by going for a jog, or knitting... I like cooking, and reading after class, too. 

Lately, though... I guess I just haven't been keeping up with any of that. To be honest—and I feel really bad admitting this—most days I just come home and sit on my bed. Still in my scrubs, even. I just... I can't seem to make myself care about doing any of those things right now. I'm sure it's just normal burnout, right? I hope I'm answering your questions okay.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired than usual, even after resting, or that you don’t have the energy to do things you normally would?

Oh, um... no, I don't think I'm physically more tired than usual. I mean, I really try to make sure I get enough sleep so I'm fully alert for my shifts. I know how important that is, and I'd never want to be sluggish at work or let my team down. 

So physically, I feel like my energy is okay. If a patient or a friend needs me, I can jump right up and do whatever they need. It's not really that I'm too exhausted to move or anything... it's more just what I said before, about not really caring to do my own hobbies when I get home. But my actual energy levels seem completely fine, I think. Does that make sense? I hope I understood your question right.
Over the past few weeks, have you found yourself feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Um... I guess... I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for. But... yeah, I suppose I have been feeling a bit down lately. 

It's kind of embarrassing to admit, but most days I wake up with this... this really heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I try my hardest to push past it, though! I promise I don't let it show. Like, I'm still smiling at my patients in Spanish, and doing my absolute best to act totally normal at the clinic. I would never want to burden anyone else with my bad moods. But... honestly, even when I'm smiling and doing my job, I feel like I'm just barely holding myself together. 

I'm sorry, I know I should be stronger than this and handle my emotions better. Am I explaining that okay?
Have you found yourself feeling more worthless or guilty than usual, even about things that wouldn’t have bothered you before?

Um... well... I guess I have been feeling a bit guilty lately. But I mean, anyone would feel bad in my situation, right? I really try so hard to be a good nurse. I study, I double-check everything... but... 

Actually, the main reason I decided to come in today is... well, I had a near-miss at the clinic recently. Nobody got hurt! I caught it in time, I promise. But ever since then, I just... I can't stop feeling like I'm a complete danger to my patients. Like I'm just a huge disappointment to my team and my professors. 

I keep telling myself that everyone makes mistakes, but... honestly? I've been feeling like that one mistake just proves I'm not cut out for this. Like I'm not meant to be a nurse at all, and maybe everyone would just be better off if I wasn't there messing things up. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds so dramatic, and I shouldn't be so hard on myself. I really don't want you to think I'm incompetent. I'm usually very careful! Is it normal to feel this awful about something that didn't even actually happen? I hope I'm not overreacting...
Can you tell me if you still enjoy the things you used to, like cooking, reading, or knitting, or if those activities don’t bring you the same satisfaction anymore?

Um... well... I try to keep up with my hobbies, I really do. I know it's important to have a good work-life balance, especially in nursing. I used to love going for a jog to clear my head, or knitting, or cooking a nice meal, or even just reading a book after my classes. 

But lately... I don't know, I guess I haven't been doing those things as much. It's not that I don't want to be a well-rounded person! It's just... lately, when I get home from my shift, I just end up sitting on my bed, still in my scrubs, and I just... I can't seem to make myself care about any of it anymore. The things that used to make me happy just feel kind of pointless right now. 

I know I should be making more of an effort to do things I enjoy. I'm sorry, I probably sound so boring and lazy right now. I promise I'm usually much more active! Is it okay that I'm just not interested in those things at the moment?
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or not wanting to live anymore?

Oh! No, no, I would never actually do anything to hurt myself. I promise! I know how selfish that would be, and I would never want to put my family or my coworkers through something like that. I definitely don't have any sort of plan or anything. 

But... um... I guess... well, it's really hard to admit this, because I know exactly how bad it sounds. But lately, I do keep having these... these thoughts. Like, sometimes I just catch myself thinking that it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up in the morning. Or if I could just kind of... disappear? Just so I wouldn't be around to mess anything up again. 

I'm so sorry, I know it's a terrible thing to say, and I feel so guilty for even letting my mind go there. I really don't mean to sound ungrateful for my life, and I swear I would never act on it! Is it... is it somewhat normal to think things like that when you're feeling this overwhelmed? I really hope I'm not scaring you or making you think I'm crazy...
Have you noticed that you feel more fatigued or that you have less energy overall, even when you haven’t been physically active?

Um... well, honestly, I haven't really noticed being more tired than usual. I mean, nursing school and clinicals are just exhausting for everyone, right? It's completely normal to feel wiped out after a long shift. 

I really try to keep my energy up, you know? I drink my coffee and push through because I know my patients and my team need me to be alert. So... I wouldn't say I'm feeling fatigued when I'm not doing anything. If anything, I probably just need to manage my time better so I can get a full eight hours of sleep. 

I hope that makes sense? I just don't want to sound like I'm complaining about being tired when everyone else in my cohort is working just as hard as I am. Am I answering that right?
Have you noticed that your thoughts have been moving more slowly than usual, or that you're physically moving more slowly, like everything feels kind of slowed down?

Um... well, I really try to stay sharp at the clinic, I promise. I always want to be as helpful and efficient as possible. But... I guess a few people there have actually made comments lately. I really hope it doesn't make me sound incompetent! 

It's just... some of the staff asked if I was feeling okay or if I was really tired, because they noticed I've been moving a bit slower than usual when I go to grab supplies. And... sometimes, if someone asks me a question, even a really simple one, it just takes me a few extra seconds to actually process it and answer them. It's like my brain is just lagging a little bit. 

I always answer them, though! I really try my best. I just feel so bad that they even noticed, because I really want to be doing a good job and not slowing anyone down. Is it normal for your brain and body to just... stall like that when you're stressed out? I hope I'm not doing too terrible of a job explaining this...
Would you say that this slowing down of your thoughts or movements has been happening most days, and has been noticeable enough that others might comment on it?

Um... yeah, I guess it has been most days lately. And like I was just saying, it definitely is noticeable enough for them to comment. The people at the clinic are the ones who keep asking if I'm tired, just because they see me moving slower when I'm getting supplies for the rooms. And... yeah, it happens pretty much every shift where it takes me a few extra seconds to answer even a simple question they ask me. 

I always apologize to them when it happens! I really, really don't want them to think I'm ignoring them or that I'm not trying my best. I'm doing everything I can to speed back up and be a good team player, I promise. I just feel awful that it's gotten to the point where they actually have to point it out. 

Is... is it okay that I'm explaining it like this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not making a bigger deal out of it than I should be.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite lately, like not feeling hungry as often or losing weight without trying?

Um... well, I try to make sure I'm eating, especially because I know how important it is to keep my strength up for clinicals. But... I guess lately, I just kind of forget to eat until really late in the day. It's not that I'm trying to starve myself or anything! I just get so busy and distracted, and I don't really feel hungry. 

When I finally do realize I haven't eaten, I usually just force down some crackers or grab another coffee, just to have something in my stomach. I know that's probably not the healthiest habit, and I'm really trying to do better about meal prepping. 

But, um... I have noticed that my work pants are getting a little loose. I definitely haven't been trying to lose weight or anything like that. I just... I guess the calories haven't been adding up the way they should. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I don't want you to think I have an eating disorder or anything, I just honestly forget sometimes.

Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in the things you used to enjoy, like cooking, reading, or knitting, or is it more that you still care about them but just don’t have the time or motivation to do them right now?

Um... well, I really do still care about them, I think. I mean, I know I should be doing them. I used to always try to clear my head after class, you know? Like, I'd go for a jog, or do some knitting, or cook a nice meal, or even just read a little bit. It was always so good for me. 

But... lately... I guess I just haven't been doing any of that. I'll get home from clinicals and I just... I just sit on my bed. Still in my scrubs. And I just sit there. It's not that I don't want to be the kind of person who does those healthy, fun things! I really do. It's just... I can't seem to make myself actually care enough to get up and do them right now. 

I know that sounds really lazy, and I promise I'm usually a very motivated person! I just... I don't know what's wrong with me. Is it normal to just lose all your drive like that when you're overwhelmed? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... I really am trying to get back into my old routine.
Would you say that this feeling of being down or depressed has been present most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Um... yeah, I guess I would say it's been most of the day, pretty much every day. For a few weeks now, at least. 

It's just... most days I wake up with this really heavy, kind of empty feeling in my chest. And I try so hard to push past it! When I'm at the clinic, I'm always smiling at the patients, especially when I'm speaking Spanish with them, and I really do try to act like everything is completely normal. I don't want anyone to think I'm bringing down the mood or that I'm not doing a good job. 

But underneath it all, I just feel like I'm... barely holding myself together. I'm so sorry, I know I shouldn't be letting it get to me this much. I really am trying to stay positive and be a good nurse. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way.
Would you say that you no longer take pleasure in the things you used to enjoy, like cooking, reading, or knitting, even though you know you should?

Um... yeah, I guess that's pretty accurate. I know we just talked about this a little bit, but... yeah. 

I used to be so good about making time for myself. I'd go for a jog, or knit, or cook something nice, or just sit and read after my classes. It was my way of clearing my head and staying balanced, you know? And I know I should still be doing those things. I really do. 

But... recently, I just can't seem to find any joy in them anymore. I come home and I just sit on my bed, still in my scrubs, and I just... I can't make myself care about doing any of it. Even though I know it would probably be good for me. 

I feel so guilty about it, honestly. I don't want to sound like I've just given up or that I'm not trying. I really am trying! I just... the enjoyment just isn't there right now. Is that okay to say? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you had any periods in the past where you felt significantly better—where most of these symptoms went away and you were able to enjoy things again, even if just for a while?

Um... no, not really. I mean, not since this whole thing started a few weeks ago. 

Before that, I was totally fine! I was doing great with my classes and clinicals, and I was really on top of everything. But since this... this heavy feeling started, it's just kind of been there the whole time. There haven't really been any days where it completely lifted or where I felt like my old self again. 

I really wish there were, though! I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or anything. I just... I haven't had a break from it yet. Is it bad that it hasn't gone away at all? I hope that's an okay answer... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.
Have you ever had a period in your life when you felt back to normal—where you were able to enjoy things again and most of these symptoms went away completely, even if just for a while?

Oh, um... I'm so sorry, did I not explain that right just a second ago? I really apologize if I'm being confusing or making you repeat yourself! 

But, um... yeah, like I think I was trying to say, I haven't really had a period where I felt back to normal. Not since this heavy feeling started a few weeks ago. I really wish I could tell you yes, because I know I should be able to just snap out of it for a day or two, and I promise I really am trying to get back to my old self! But it's just been pretty constant. 

I hope that answers it better this time? I'm so sorry again if I wasn't clear before, I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time in your life when you felt persistently down or lost interest in things for a period of at least two weeks?

Um... no, actually. Before this started a few weeks ago, I've never really felt like this. 

I mean, sure, I'd get stressed about exams or clinicals sometimes—everyone gets a little overwhelmed, right? But I always bounced right back. I've never had a time where I felt down or lost interest in things for two whole weeks straight. I've always prided myself on being a really upbeat, positive person, always keeping busy and staying on top of things. 

I really hope it's a good sign that this hasn't happened before? Like, maybe it means it's just a weird phase and it'll go away soon? I'm really trying my best to just get back on track so I don't let anyone down. Does that sound right to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right history.
Have you ever experienced a time before this current period where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks at a time?

Oh, gosh, um... I feel terrible, I think you might have just asked me that, right? I am so, so sorry if I'm not answering things the right way or if I'm making this difficult for you! I'm usually much better at listening, I promise. 

But, um, to answer your question... no, I really haven't. Before these last few weeks, I've never had a time where I felt down or lost interest in things for that long. Never more than two weeks, or even close to that, really. I was always the one cheering everyone else up! 

I really hope I'm not wasting your time by repeating myself. Am I doing okay? I just want to be as helpful as possible for you.
